cases.name: Lan Thi Rawls
cases.about:
Lan was a beloved member of the Aulander, NC community known as the “Tootsie Roll Lady” due to her habit of giving children candy while out walking. 

Her obituary said, "She was born on February 7, 1943 in Vietnam to her father, Nguyễn Văn Viêm and mother, Dương Thị Vẻ. In 1975, she emigrated to the United States at the end of the Vietnam War and settled in Aulander after meeting her husband, Robert McCoy Rawls. She and Robert welcomed their daughter, Cathy in June 1976. In 1982, their family grew as Lan’s three daughters, Nancy, Amanda, and Frances, from a previous marriage were finally reunited after years of separation due to the war.

Many remember Lan working in her flower garden, something that brought her much joy and comfort. If she wasn’t in the garden, she would be working on house repairs, painting, or climbing on top of the roof to lay tar.

She also loved sewing, which can be seen in all the beautiful things she hand-made, from curtains to bedding to Christmas stockings.

To know Lan, was to love her. She was a person that touched so many people’s hearts, whether it was through a fun conversation or bringing food to a neighbor. When she got to a point in which she couldn’t visit others anymore, she ALWAYS made sure that whoever came by the house for a visit that they left with a Mountain Dew and some cookies. That is who she was. Her whole life was devoted to her children, grandchildren and great-grandchildren. She did her best to build a foundation in which all her family knew how much she loved them."
cases.narrative: Lan would leave her door unlocked for the night caregiver to arrive, and then would call her daughter, who lived out of state, to let her know they had locked up for the night. When that phone call didn’t come, her daughter first called the caregiver and then a nearby relative who found the crime scene. That relative discovered her caretaker Rochelle Harrell “bleeding profusely”, and Rawls dead in the hallway with her body on fire. Her autopsy reportedly says her arms were bound in tape, and that she had thermal injuries involving 44% of her body. It says she died from asphyxia with smoke inhalation and injuries due to the fire.
